title: An aligned table in a text block

blocks.text: The page's first best practice uses `\s` for alignment:

Trailing spaces in a text block are stripped, so a table whose cells are padded to equal width loses the padding at the end of each line, unless the line ends with `\s`: the spaces before it are then no longer trailing.

Write `AlignedTable.lines(List<List<String>> rows)`. Every row has the same number of cells. Return the content lines you would write inside the text block (no delimiters, no indentation), joined by `\n`:

items: each cell is padded with spaces on the right to its column's width, the length of the widest cell of that column in any row;
cells are separated by one space;
if a line then ends with a space, that last space is written `\s`.

cases.says: Each cell is padded to its column's width, and a line that ends in padding writes its last space as \s.
A column is as wide as its widest cell in any row, not only in the header.
Padding after the last column is fenced with \s on every line that has it, so the compiler cannot strip it.
An empty cell is written as spaces of its column's width.

concepts: \s fences padding at the end of a line, which keeps columns aligned in a text block table.
